v.why: Lowering an excessively high learning rate rescues training (exps 7,8,9,19), unlike at low lr.
Very small learning rates are undertrained in 243 epochs, so raising them helps (exps 1,11).
Raising an already large learning rate causes divergence (exp 14).
Shallower nets are more stable at high learning rates (exps 76,79).
Adding depth at high lr destabilizes training (exp 70).
Narrower networks tolerate large learning rates better (exps 52,53,60).
Strong L2 already underfits, and more hurts (exps 89,87).
More update steps help at high lr on segment (exps 32,37,40).
Wider nets learn faster at small learning rates (exps 41,44,48).

raw:
Hypotheses drawn from the 100 experiments, with the clearest signals first:

- **Learning rate down at high lr:** Experiments 7, 8, 9, 19 show large gains (+30 to +69 on segment) when lowering lr from 0.0774 or above. At low lr, lowering it gives small or negative changes.
- **Learning rate up at low lr:** Experiments 1 and 11 show big gains at lr of 1e-5 to 3.59e-5 (up to +31 on vehicle), while at high lr (exp 14) raising it hurts badly.
- **Depth down at high lr:** Experiments 76 and 79 show gains for depth 3→2 at lr of 0.0774 or higher, and experiment 70 shows depth up hurting at lr 0.278.
- **Alpha up at high alpha:** Experiment 89 (alpha 0.129) shows a large loss, and experiment 87 (mid-high lr) also shows one. Alpha down at high alpha gives gains (92, 93, 91).
- **Width down at high lr:** Experiments 52, 53, 60 show gains, with exp 57 also positive.
- **Width up at low lr:** Experiment 41 and, on vehicle, 44 and 48 show small gains.
- **Batch size down at high lr:** Experiments 32, 37, 40 show gains on segment, with phoneme mixed, so this is a weaker signal.
